task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n>=1, omega a smooth positive Hermitian (1,1)-form, and dV a smooth strictly positive probability volume. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi)) partial barpartial. For real continuous F, c_0(F)>0 is the unique normalization scalar such that a bounded omega-psh solution u satisfies (omega+dd^c u)^n=c_0(F) exp(F) dV. Put B_0(F)=log c_0(F). Equivalently, for n>=2 one may use the fixed-density Gauduchon formula
B_0(F)=n log inf_gamma [integral_X omega wedge gamma^(n-1)]/[integral_X (exp(F)dV/gamma^n)^(1/n) gamma^n],
where gamma ranges over smooth positive Hermitian metrics satisfying dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0. In dimension one B_0(F)=log integral_X omega-log integral_X exp(F)dV.
Let A_0(F) be the Borel probability measures nu such that B_0(G)<=B_0(F)-integral_X(G-F)dnu for every real continuous G.
Question: does A_0(F) consist of a single probability measure for every compact complex X, every Hermitian omega and every real F in C(X)? Equivalently, prove Gateaux differentiability of the concave B_0 at every continuous F, or find an exceptional continuous logarithmic density with two different supporting probabilities. This demands uniqueness of the induced probability, and does not require uniqueness of an auxiliary maximizing current.
Known background: supporting sets are nonempty, convex, weakly compact and absolutely continuous. They are singletons for smooth F, for closed Kahler omega, and on a dense G_delta of C(X). In dimension n>=2 supporting probabilities are normalized determinant-weighted measures of exact maximizing positive dd^c-closed (n-1,n-1) currents T with integral_X omega wedge T=1. In an omega-unitary frame write sigma_T=omega wedge T and beta wedge T=(1/n)tr(B_beta P_T) sigma_T, with P_T>=0, tr P_T=n. The weighted determinant measure is Gamma_F(T)=(exp(F)dV/omega^n)^(1/n)(det P_T)^(1/n) sigma_T and is absolutely continuous. Maximizers attain Gamma_F(T)(X)=exp(-B_0(F)/n); their supporting probabilities are Gamma_F(T)/Gamma_F(T)(X). Their densities have uniform L^p bounds on bounded sets of F for 1<p<n/(n-1), and at the endpoint if lower mass is positive. Compactness or these bounds alone do not imply uniqueness. Near-maximizers may have unbounded higher determinant moments even for fixed smooth data.
task.completionCriteria: Resolve the full every-continuous-density singleton question by complete proof, or give a compact Hermitian example with a real continuous F and two demonstrably distinct probabilities satisfying the defining supporting inequality for all continuous G. Preserve the nonsingular reference zero and strictly positive exp(F). Smooth-density differentiability, dense generic uniqueness, weak compactness, uniqueness of scalar or potential, and a result for only Kahler backgrounds do not close the question. Any linearized weak operator or product used must be defined and justified rather than assumed. Verify external mathematical premises at primary sources and independently reconstruct the proof.

# P16: statement-only continuous positive Hessian targets

These are root-developed restricted candidates. They are not an autonomous
discovery or a solution of the unrestricted every-continuous-density P16.
Use dd^c=i partial barpartial/(2pi). Every potential is its genuine canonical
upper representative. Preserve nonsingular reference zero and strictly
positive exp(F). No proof, author paper or prior report is supplied.

A. Let X be any connected compact complex n-fold,n>=2, omega smooth
strictly positive, dV a smooth positive probability, F real continuous.
Suppose an ACTUAL bounded genuine solution u of the original normalized
equation has distributional complex Hessian sigma=omega+dd^c u represented
by a continuous everywhere strictly positive real(1,1) form. Then A_0(F)
is a singleton and, for every real continuous H,
 d/dt|t=0 B_0(F+tH)=-integral H dnu_F.
No full real C2 representative or Holder/Dini modulus is assumed. No
existence of such a Hessian for general continuous F is claimed.
Prove actual bounded-product linearization, signed admissibility,
L_sigma=tr_sigma(dd^c h) and annihilation of every support, with no
undefined rough-current product.

B. For ANY continuous positive Hermitian form sigma on such X and EVERY
p>2n, L_sigma:W^(2,p)(X)->L^p(X,dV) is Fredholm of index0, kernel precisely
the constants, range annihilator of dimension1 in L^(p/(p-1)). The
continuous-coefficient extension is an AUTHOR PROOF OBLIGATION, not a
permitted black box. Supply the coefficient-freezing estimate, the
maximum principle at actual W^(2,p) regularity, and the global Fredholm
argument. Do not invoke a smooth core for an unspecified rough generator,
differentiate continuous coefficients or grant rough adjoint uniqueness.
Use the ORIGINAL supplied L^q bounds, for1<q<n/(n-1), to identify every
support through a justified duality exponent and extension from smooth
tests. Absolute continuity alone is not assumed to imply uniqueness.

C. Let Y be ANY connected compact Hermitian k-fold,k>=1 with smooth
kappa and integral kappa^k=1; w is Fubini--Study probability on P1.
For a>0, smooth b(x)>0 and ANY continuous A(x)>0 on P1 with integral Aw=a,
put X=P1 timesY, omega=aw+b kappa, dV=w kappa^k,
F=log[(k+1)Ab^k]. Then c_0(F)=1 and the unique actual support is
 (A/a)w tensor nu_kappa,
where nu_kappa is the smooth positive stationary probability of the
smooth complex Laplacian L_kappa; for k=1 it is simply kappa.
Prove an actual bounded genuine solution and its continuous positive
Hessian, and identify the support for EVERY continuous G in the defining
inequality. Stationarity on separated tests alone is insufficient.

D. Give the explicit non-Kahler3fold instance Y=(C2 without0)/<z->2z>,
kappa the unit-volume rescaling of |z|^-2 dd^c|z|^2, b=2+tau on P1,
and A=a+epsilon[f(tau)-integral f(tau)w],0<epsilon<a,
f(0)=0,f(t)=1/log(e/|t|) for0<|t|<=1. This yields a smooth genuinely
nonclosed background and a continuous everywhere positive exp(F), with F
neither Dini nor Holder of any positive order. Identify the unique support
explicitly, verify positivity, the lack of Dini regularity, the Hopf
stationary volume and non-Kahler property. Preserve reference zero.

E. A requires the continuous positive Hessian hypothesis and gives no
proof for arbitrary continuous F. C's two-curve specialization overlaps
the nonsingular specialization of an existing product-adjoint argument;
no literature priority is claimed. No unrestricted P16 counterexample or
completion follows from A--D; no Frechet differentiability is asserted.
Reject any inference of full original completion.

Precise permitted imported foundations, not proofs of A--E:

7. A smooth positive Hermitian metric on a connected compact complex

8. Smooth Stokes, elementary Hermitian determinant and block-matrix
